speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. Your history of a painful, swollen left ankle followed by knee issues and urinary pain suggests a systemic inflammatory condition; have you noticed any skin rashes or eye redness recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your sexual history and symptoms of urethritis, knee swelling, and a prior ankle attack, could you describe the specific type of discharge from your penis or any eye irritation you might have? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Gram Stain, and Urethral Swab for NAAT (Gonorrhea/Chlamydia).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Protein Negative, Blood Negative, WBC 12–16/hpf, RBC 1–2/hpf; Urine Gram Stain: Not performed per available data; Urethral Swab for NAAT (Gonorrhea/Chlamydia): Not performed per available data. Note: Existing data includes Urinalysis with 12–16 WBC/hpf, bilateral conjunctival inflammation, and right knee synovial fluid analysis (Cloudy appearance, 26,000/mm3 leukocytes, 75% neutrophils, Gram stain negative).

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history reported. Social history: Sexually active with multiple partners, inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Patient
text: Experiences anxiety; denies recent flu-like symptoms, denies any known sexually transmitted infections. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).
